links.comparator_used: Same DeepSeek-V3.2 models (base and reasoning) without RAG, assessed on internal retrieval datasets and external test datasets
links.outcome: Classification performance on the subjective severity tasks
links.effect: RAG significantly improved both models on internal retrieval datasets (P<.05) but not on external test datasets (P>.05). Adding RAG to V3.2-R lowered accuracy to 81%, versus 86% without RAG.
links.tradeoff: Adding RAG to V3.2-R degraded performance on external data, suggesting potential noise interference. The authors say the finding is tied to their setup and current retrieval implementation.
links.quote: Crucially, while RAG significantly improved both models' performance on internal retrieval datasets (P<.05), this benefit did not generalize to external test datasets (P>.05).

links.comparator_used: High-speed base model V3.2-B, which answers directly without CoT reasoning
links.outcome: Accuracy and F1-score on subjective severity assessment
links.effect: V3.2-B reached 56.6% accuracy on severity grading, with recall of 0 for minor anomalies. V3.2-R with CoT reached 86% accuracy and F1-score=0.75 on external data without RAG.
links.quote: In contrast, the V3.2-R model utilizing CoT reasoning achieved superior robustness (86% accuracy and F1-score=0.75) on external data without RAG; notably, introducing RAG to V3.2-R degraded performance to 81%, suggesting potential noise interference.

links.outcome: Performance on subjective severity assessment, with factual extraction tasks as a contrast
links.effect: The reasoning-enhanced V3.2-R reached 86% accuracy and F1-score=0.75 on external data. V3.2-B scored 56.6% accuracy on severity but above 90% accuracy and F1-score on factual tasks.
links.tradeoff: The base model remains efficient for factual classification, so the authors recommend a fast-slow split rather than replacing it.
